tagline: Clear filters to compute totals and percentages regardless of slicers

slides.title: Why Remove Filters?
slides.body: When a slicer or row context filters the data, your measure only sees a subset. ALL() and REMOVEFILTERS() clear those filters so you can compute grand totals, denominators for %, or cross-category comparisons.
slides.keyPoint: CALCULATE([Sales], ALL(DimDate)) ignores any date slicer and always returns sales for all time.

slides.title: Data — User Slicer Set to 2024
slides.caption: Without ALL, measures only see the filtered 2024 rows
slides.note: Active filter context: Year = 2024. [Total Sales] = 610,000 (only 2024 visible)

slides.title: Three Related Measures
slides.code:
-- Respects the year slicer
[Total Sales] = SUM(Sales[Revenue])

-- Ignores the year slicer entirely
[All Time Sales] =
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Sales[Revenue]),
    ALL(DimDate)
)

-- Current year as % of all-time total
[% of Total] =
DIVIDE([Total Sales], [All Time Sales])
slides.annotation: ALL(DimDate) clears every filter on DimDate — the Year slicer no longer affects [All Time Sales], allowing a meaningful denominator for the % measure.

slides.title: Result with Year = 2024 Selected
slides.caption: Even though the slicer is on 2024, [All Time Sales] sees all years

slides.title: ALL vs REMOVEFILTERS — The Difference
bullets: ALL(Table) — dual purpose: clears filters AND can return the full table as a result (usable in FILTER or RANKX)
REMOVEFILTERS(Table) — only removes filters, cannot return a table (cleaner intent, recommended in CALCULATE)
ALL(Table[Column]) — removes filter only from one specific column, other column filters stay active
ALLEXCEPT(Table, Col1, Col2) — removes ALL filters on a table EXCEPT the columns listed
slides.keyPoint: Exam rule: use REMOVEFILTERS when intent is purely to clear a filter inside CALCULATE. Use ALL when you also need the full table returned (e.g., RANKX(ALL(DimProduct), [Sales])).

slides.title: Common ALL Patterns
bullets: % of Grand Total: DIVIDE([Sales], CALCULATE([Sales], ALL(FactSales)))
Running Total: CALCULATE([Sales], FILTER(ALL(DimDate), DimDate[Date] <= MAX(DimDate[Date])))
slides.warning: ALL inside CALCULATE removes the filter, but measure-level filter tables and explicit visual-level filters can have higher precedence. Know the filter context precedence order for the PL-300 exam.
